name: Jeff Bhasker
notes: Berklee-trained jazz-piano arranger turned big-anthem producer. The drum claim is about size and attack rather than pattern: "huge, reverberant, slow-attack drums — either a played kit in a big room or a heavily processed machine kit — with the backbeat as an event rather than a bed; stomps, claps and gang percussion for the anthem mode." So the snare is `soft` transient under a `large` tail with a very low ghost probability (an event does not repeat), the velocity tiers are the widest-spread here, the kick density drops to 1—3, `hihat.continuous` is false at `fillDensity` 0.08 with no rolls, and the perc lanes are the stomp/clap/gang set at high density. The 808 is authored because the entry names its lineage precisely: "from the *808s & Heartbreak* lineage — long, tuned 808 sub notes used harmonically rather than rhythmically", so `bass808` is `counter_riff` with a `legato` sustain, a near-zero `slideProb` and no `slidesPer4Bars` — the 808 here is a held chord tone, which is the opposite of a trap 808 — while the "organ/synth bass pedals under the anthem choruses" stay as the bassline. Harmony follows "extended chords, gospel plagal cadences and modulating final choruses; minor-key anthems with a major III as the lift", so the IV—I and III-bearing families lead and the extension spread is rich. "His arrangements favour a wordless massed vocal or choir as the countermelody" and "toplines are given room by keeping the midrange sparse" is the `sustain_pad` counter over a low `densityPerBar`. ⚠ `confidence` is medium and the research says why: "specific drum/bass parameters inferred from the documented records he made". Every drum probability, the humanize numbers, the harmonic weights and `bpm.mode` 110 (the midpoint of the stated 90—130 anthem core) are INFERRED. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“from the *808s & Heartbreak* lineage — long, tuned 808 sub notes used harmonically rather than rhythmically, and organ/synth bass pedals under the anthem choruses.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord.
